ai.description: *Sitana thondalu* is a small lizard reaching 50–60 mm snout-vent length. It features a brownish body with a dark-spotted dorsal pattern and a distinctive, large, tri-colored dewlap in breeding males.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Sitana thondalu* is uniquely distinguished by its distinctively elongated, tri-colored dewlap (blue, black, and white) that extends beyond the chest when fully flared.
ai.habitat: *Sitana thondalu* inhabits the scrub forests and rocky outcrops of the Deccan Plateau, typically found in arid, open landscapes with sparse vegetation at low elevations.
ai.behavior: The Nagarjuna Sagar fan-throated lizard is diurnal, spending its active hours foraging for small insects and displaying its vibrant throat fan to attract mates or rivals.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Sitana thondalu* is oviparous, laying clutches of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Sitana thondalu* is endemic to the Deccan Plateau in India, primarily occurring in the states of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh at low to moderate elevations.
